Until the Meiji period it was called “Mishima Daimyōjin”; it was given its current name in Meiji, but is still called '''Mishima Shrine''' today. {{nihongo|'''Yagokorōoichihiko Shrine'''|八心大市比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

It enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamazumi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Kami}}, and {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|az|Kaqutsuçi|de|Kagutsuchi|es|Kagutsuchi|fa|کاگو-تسوچی|fr|Kagutsuchi|it|Kagutsuchi|ja|カグツチ|mni|ꯀꯒꯨ-ꯁꯨꯆꯤ|pl|Kagutsuchi|ru|Кагуцути|sv|Kagutsuchi|ta|ககுட்சூசி|tr|Kagutsuchi|uk|Кагу-цуті|zh|迦具土|qid=Q1640658|lt=Kagutsuchi-no-Kami}} as principal deities, and {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}} as a merged deity<ref name="p330">''Toyama Prefecture Shrine Gazette'' (published November 10, 1983 by Toyama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines), p.330.</ref>.

Spring festival is May 5, annual-year festival is February 20, autumn festival is October 4, and Niiname-sai is November 26. Special rites include the Chinowa rite (June 30)<ref name="tt" /> and Jijin Festival (June 25; sacred bamboo is set around the shrine and the event is celebrated with songs and dance)<ref name="tt" /><ref name="p330" />.

The precinct area is 4,000 tsubo, with 13 million ujiko<ref name="p330" />.

== History ==
There are various theories on foundation: one says it was invited to Sakurai-shō Mikkaichi during the reign of {{ill|Empress Kōken|Q232955|qid=Q232955}}<ref name="p330" />; another says a {{ill|Gohei|Q1011372|qid=Q1011372}} flew from a mountaintop in Karezawa Village to the east (present Karezawa, Kurobe), stayed in Mikkaichi, and when locals enshrined it, three {{ill|Idols in Shinto|Q11588751|qid=Q11588751}} appeared, and so it was revered as “Mishima Daimyōjin”<ref name="rs">''A Historical Walk of Toyama Prefecture'' (Yamakawa Publishing, issued March 31, 2013, 1st ed., 3rd printing), pp.26-27.</ref>. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is ranked as a small shrine<ref name="p330" />.

From old times it has been deeply revered from nearby and surrounding areas as a deity of abundant harvests, medicine and brewing, fire protection, and foremost divine protection<ref name="rs" /><ref name="p330" />. It is said that in earlier times imperial messengers were sent, offerings and sacred mirrors were dedicated, and rites were carried out with great solemnity<ref name="p330" />.

One tradition says the name “Mishima Daimyōjin” comes from {{ill|Sano Genzaemon|Q11385069|qid=Q11385069}} in the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, who revered {{ill|Mishima Taisha|Q650772|qid=Q650772|lt=Mishima Shrine}} in Izu, brought a cherry branch from there, and grafted it onto a tree in this shrine’s precinct. The shrine crest is a cherry emblem called “Sakurai-zakura.”

Originally it stood about 500 m north of the current site (Kayadō<ref name="kn2">''Commemorative Journal II: Exploring Changes in Architectural Culture in Kurobe City'' (February 20, 2008, Toyama Prefecture Architects Association Kurobe Branch), p.14.</ref>), but after shrine buildings, treasures, and old documents were lost to fire in the Nagao clan’s warfare during the {{ill|Eiroku|ca|Eiroku|ckb|ئێیرۆکو|fa|ایروکو|fr|Ère Eiroku|ja|永禄|ko|에이로쿠|ru|Эйроку|simple|Eiroku|sr|Еироку|sv|Eiroku|tr|Eiroku|zh|永祿|qid=Q1143341}} era ({{ill|1558|Q6601|qid=Q6601}}-{{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}})<ref name="rs" /><ref name="p330" />, it was moved to the present site in {{ill|1580|Q6712|qid=Q6712}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 8). After major reconstruction of shrine buildings in {{ill|1688|Q7671|qid=Q7671}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 1)<ref name="kn2" />, it reverted to its pre-Kamakura shrine name “Yagokorōoichihiko Shrine” after the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}<ref name="p330" />, and in August {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6) was ranked as the first prefectural shrine in the lower Shin-kawa region<ref>''Mishima Community Center New Building Commemoration: Then and Now of Mishima Town in Photos'' (September 1, 1995, Mishima Town Neighborhood Association), p.122.</ref>. On {{ill|June 24|Q2665|qid=Q2665}}, {{ill|1925|Q18107|qid=Q18107}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 14), Shinmei Shrine in Tenjinshin, {{ill|Ishida|Q11587014|qid=Q11587014|lt=Ishida Village}} (enshrining Amaterasu-Ōmikami), and household earth deities were {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=merged}} (an earth mound was built under the large zelkova at this time)<ref name="p330" /><ref name="tt">''Toyama Encyclopedia, Vol. 2'' (August 1, 1994, Kita-Nippon Shimbun), p.978.</ref>. On {{ill|October 25|Q2954|qid=Q2954}}, {{ill|1942|Q18625|qid=Q18625}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 17), the current shrine buildings using cypress from imperial Kiso timber were completed (transfer rites took place the day before, {{ill|October 24|Q2955|qid=Q2955}})<ref name="p330" /><ref>''Mishima Community Center New Building Commemoration: Then and Now of Mishima Town in Photos'' (September 1, 1995, Mishima Town Neighborhood Association), p.124.</ref>. The precinct was expanded at the same time<ref name="kn2" />. Since then, grounds and facilities have been developed progressively<ref name="p330" />.

From {{ill|2020|Q25337|qid=Q25337}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 2), work was carried out to replace the copper roof plating, completed in November {{ill|2021|Q49628|qid=Q49628}} (Reiwa 3)<ref>''{{ill|The Kitanippon Shimbun|Q11401857|qid=Q11401857}}'', Jan 17, 2022, p.6, “Our Town from the Sky: Mikkaichi, Kurobe City.”</ref>.

== Facilities ==
[[File:Mishima-no-Ookeyaki019.jpg|thumb|Mishima’s great zelkova]]
The precinct has been designated a Kurobe City {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}} since {{ill|July 11|Q2701|qid=Q2701}}, {{ill|1955|Q18577|qid=Q18577}}. “Sakurai no Bakefuji” and “Mishima no Ōkeyaki” in detached precinct land (once part of the large original grounds but later separated) are city-designated natural monuments (designated {{ill|February 1|Q2312|qid=Q2312}}, {{ill|1965|Q2650|qid=Q2650}} and {{ill|September 28|Q2883|qid=Q2883}}, {{ill|1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434}}, respectively)<ref>[https://www.pref.toyama.jp/documents/14279/07-kurobe.pdf Cultural Properties of Kurobe City No.7] (Toyama Prefecture, accessed December 10, 2022)</ref>.

{{ill|Chicken|Q780|qid=Q780|lt=Chickens}} are treated as {{ill|Shinshi|Q10444973|qid=Q10444973}}, and nearby people reportedly did not eat either meat or eggs<ref name="tt" />. There also remains an {{ill|Ema (Shinto)|Q687288|qid=Q687288}} of a chicken dedicated in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 2 ({{ill|1689|Q7674|qid=Q7674}}).
